item.title: 'Mortified' McInnes takes responsibility for Rangers' European exit
item.description: Manager Derek McInnes says he takes "full responsibility" for Rangers' "embarrassing" Conference League exit at the hands of Jablonec.

item.title: Man City and Aston Villa to face champions PSG
item.description: European champions Paris St-Germain will face Premier League duo Manchester City and Aston Villa in the league phase of this season's Champions League.

item.title: Chelsea agree £7.5m fee for Villa's Martinez
item.description: Chelsea agree a £7.5m fee to sign Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez.

item.title: Arsenal continue Alvarez pursuit - Friday's gossip
item.description: Arsenal continue pursuit to sign Julian Alvarez, Manchester City target Everton's Iliman Ndiaye and Aston Villa make direct contact to sign Rafael Leao.

item.title: Ipswich sign Argentina World Cup winner Palacios
item.description: Argentina midfielder Exequiel Palacios becomes the first World Cup winner to sign for Ipswich Town after joining from Bayer Leverkusen.

item.title: Uefa preparing criminal legal action against Infantino
item.description: Uefa is pursuing criminal proceedings against Fifa president Gianni Infantino over the scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup.

item.title: Sutton's predictions v Royal Blood drummer Ben Thatcher
item.description: BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton takes on Royal Blood drummer Ben Thatcher, plus the BBC readers and AI with his predictions for this weekend's Premier League fixtures.

item.title: Have expensively-assembled Rangers improved at all under McInnes?
item.description: After crashing out of the Conference League, questions are mounting for Derek McInnes at Rangers, writes Tom English.

item.title: Arsenal only likely exit for Alvarez as striker skips training
item.description: Julian Alvarez has not attended Atletico Madrid training since being told privately that the club would not sell him to Barcelona.

item.title: Villa sign Goretzka - what went wrong at Bayern and what will he bring?
item.description: Aston Villa complete the signing of former Bayern Munich midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free transfer.

item.title: Carragher facing bankruptcy petition over unpaid tax claim
item.description: Former Liverpool and England player turned pundit Jamie Carragher faces being declared bankrupt over an unpaid tax bill.

item.title: Leyton Orient criticise badge on new Wrexham kit
item.description: Leyton Orient criticise Wrexham and their celebrity owners, Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac, for putting a badge on their new kit that mirrors their own.

item.title: Liverpool close in on £120m deal for PSG's Barcola
item.description: Liverpool are close to agreeing a deal with Paris St-Germain for Bradley Barcola - adding to the doubts surrounding Cody Gakpo's Anfield future.

item.title: Celtic crash out of Champions League after humiliating defeat to LASK
item.description: Despite leading 4-0 on aggregate, Celtic are humiliated by LASK as they lose the second leg of their Champions League play-off 5-1 and are knocked out 5-4 on aggregate in Austria to miss out on the main draw of the Champions League for a second successive season.

item.title: Fenerbahce back in the Champions League after 18 years
item.description: Goals from Vedat Muriqi and Archie Brown prove to be enough for Fenerbahce to get past Lyon and in to the league stage of the Champions League.

item.title: Viking reach Champions League for first time with victory over Dinamo Zagreb
item.description: Viking shock Dinamo Zagreb with a 3-1 win to book their place in the Champions League.

item.title: Slovan Bratislava through in Champions League after extra-time brilliance
item.description: A brilliant flick over the keeper from Cristian Martinez in extra time is enough to get Slovan Bratislava past Celje and in to the Champions League.

item.title: AEK Athens cruise past Levski Sofia with dominant 4-0 win
item.description: AEK Athens are through to the Champions League with a comfortable 4-0 win against Levski Sofia.

item.title: Stunning comeback sees Sabah reach Champions League for the first time
item.description: Azerbaijan side Sabah fight back from 4-2 down on aggregate to beat Hapoel Be'er Sheva of Israel 6-4 on aggregate to secure their place in the main draw of the Champions League for the first time.

item.title: Bodo/Glimt thrash NEC to ease into Champions League main draw
item.description: Bodo/Glimt reach the main draw of the Champions League for a second successive season after beating Dutch side NEC Nijmegen 3-0 in the second leg of their play-off, qualifying 6-1 on aggregate.

item.title: 'I'm very proud of this' - Fernandes wins PFA player of the year

item.title: 'Truly honoured' - Shaw wins PFA player of the year award
item.description: Manchester City forward Khadija Shaw reacts to winning her second PFA player of the year award in three seasons.

item.title: 'A huge award' - O'Reilly named PFA young player of the year
item.description: Manchester City and England full-back Nico O'Reilly says "it feels amazing" after receiving the 2026 PFA young player of the year award.

item.title: 'Super proud' - Smith wins consecutive PFA young player of the year
item.description: Arsenal's Olivia Smith wants to "keep setting standards high" as she receives her second consecutive PFA young player of the year award.

item.title: Palmer impresses as Chelsea edge past Fulham to give Alonso first win
item.description: Cole Palmer scores and sets up Joao Pedro as Chelsea give Xabi Alonso a winning start against Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham at Craven Cottage in the Premier League.

item.title: 'To have a good team, we need a great Cole' - Alonso on Palmer
item.description: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso praises Cole Palmer's "responsibility, maturity and freedom" after a goal and an assist from the playmaker seals a 3-2 victory over Fulham at Craven Cottage. In Alonso's first Premier League match in charge, the Spaniard insists his new squad can achieve "special things" this season.

item.title: Fulham deserved more in Chelsea defeat - Arbeloa
item.description: Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa says his side deserved "a little bit more" following their 3-2 home defeat by Chelsea but is encouraged by the "character and personality" shown in his first Premier League game in charge.

item.title: Why Herrera is playing for free in Spanish third division
